Subject: Draft review — 3 stars

Three stars. There’s a lot I like about my grooming van, but getting a plumbing problem sorted out was much harder than it needed to be.

I’m a mobile dog groomer in Halifax, and Harbourline did the fitout on my Transit in August. First, credit where it’s due: the stainless tub and ramp are honestly the best thing about the van. The dogs walk right in, and that makes a real difference when you spend your day persuading large, damp animals to cooperate. I’m genuinely happy with that part of the work.

On October 27, a fitting on the hot water line let go while I was grooming Moose, a 110-pound Bernese. Water went all over the floor and into the cabinet. Moose sat in the tub through the whole thing like a king surveying his new waterfront property. Absolutely unbothered. I was the one screaming. There was only one professional in that van at that moment, and unfortunately he was the dog.

I had to towel him off and send him home half finished, then cancel the rest of that day. The van was off the road from October 27 to November 6, and I lost six bookings on top of the remainder of the day it happened. When your workplace is also your vehicle, that’s a pretty rough stretch.

The leak itself wasn’t what upset me most. Stuff breaks. What bothered me was the response before anyone had looked at it. I was told these lines don’t just let go and that it was usually caused by running the heater dry or hanging things off the pipe, which would count as user error and wouldn’t be covered. I hadn’t done either of those things. The pipe is behind a cabinet door.

The earliest appointment offered was November 3, with a $180 diagnostic fee. Being faced with that fee and a suggestion of user error while cancelling clients was frustrating, especially with a 12-month workmanship warranty on the invoice.

To Glenn’s credit, he did own it in the end. When the van was ready on November 6, he said the outlet compression fitting was a cheaper one his supplier had substituted, and that it was on them. He replaced all the fittings on the hot side and took the $180 charge off. That matters, and it’s only fair to include it here.

So this isn’t a “everything was terrible” review. The tub and ramp are great, and Harbourline ultimately put the plumbing right. But the initial response and the time off the road are why I can’t give more than three stars.

For other groomers or trades considering a fitout, my advice is to get the warranty details in writing, including how diagnostic charges work and how a suspected warranty problem will be assessed. Mine had a written warranty, but I wish I’d clarified that process before I needed it.

Happy with the tub. Glad the repair was taken care of. Would have really appreciated less jumping to user error along the way. Moose, meanwhile, appears to have no complaints about his pool party.
